title: Defense Systems Analyst (I) (LtCol to Capt) FMOS, DC P&R
raw_text:
16.     MOS 8852, Defense Systems Analyst (I) (LtCol to Capt) FMOS, DC P&R

    a. Summary. The Defense Systems Analyst participates in studies and
analyses of force structures, weapon system mixes, and cost effectiveness
comparisons that support resource allocation decisions in programming and
analysis sections located at top management levels and research and
development activities.

    b. Prerequisites.       Security requirement:   secret security clearance
eligibility.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Defense Systems Analysis Curriculum
Number 817 at Naval Postgraduate School or equivalent postgraduate degree at
a comparable accredited institution.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Participates in studies and analysis of material requirements and
military force structures, comparisons of weapon systems, and weapon system
mixes.

        (2) Uses empirical data, economic theory, organizational theory,
decision analysis, and mathematical and statistical techniques to establish
the comparative factors and alternatives available to the decision maker.

        (3) Provides technical support to associated staff sections in the
review and evaluation of studies and analyses completed by other agencies.

        (4) Reviews and evaluates systems cost estimates to include
developmental, production, and life cycle costs.

        (5) Assists the decision maker in defining problems, identifying
alternatives, and formulating recommendations.

        (6) Performs cost effectiveness and cost benefit analysis to support
resource allocation decisions.

        (7) Performs technical liaison with other military and governmental
agencies that conduct analytical or evaluation studies.

        (8) Performs any or all of the above duties and tasks in programming
and analysis sections located at top management levels and research and
development activities.




                                         1-358                        Enclosure (1)
 1147                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Management Analysts 13-1111.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

matches: Perform system lifecycle cost analysis and develop component studies.

The Defense Systems Analyst participates in studies and analyses of force structures, weapon system mixes, and cost effectiveness comparisons that support resource allocation decisions in programming and analysis sections located at top management levels and research and development activities.
Participate in the development of specifications for equipment, products, or substitute materials.
d. Duties (1) Participates in studies and analysis of material requirements and military force structures, comparisons of weapon systems, and weapon system mixes.
Compile, analyze, and report data to explain economic phenomena and forecast market trends, applying mathematical models and statistical techniques.

(2) Uses empirical data, economic theory, organizational theory, decision analysis, and mathematical and statistical techniques to establish the comparative factors and alternatives available to the decision maker.
Direct and review the work of staff members, including survey support staff and interviewers who gather survey data.
(3) Provides technical support to associated staff sections in the review and evaluation of studies and analyses completed by other agencies.
Estimate costs for system or component implementation and operation.
(4) Reviews and evaluates systems cost estimates to include developmental, production, and life cycle costs.
Formulate recommendations, policies, or plans to solve economic problems or to interpret markets.
(5) Assists the decision maker in defining problems, identifying alternatives, and formulating recommendations.
Prepare cost-benefit and return-on-investment analyses to aid in decisions on system implementation.
(6) Performs cost effectiveness and cost benefit analysis to support resource allocation decisions.
Hire, supervise, or evaluate engineers, technicians, researchers, or other staff.
(7) Performs technical liaison with other military and governmental agencies that conduct analytical or evaluation studies.
Assign, coordinate, and review work and activities of programming personnel.
(8) Performs any or all of the above duties and tasks in programming and analysis sections located at top management levels and research and development activities.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
